sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
sites.blurb: Rim of the 21 km Shackleton crater, astride 0°E.
sites.why: The classic case: permanent shadow metres away, but the rim itself sees the Sun for most of the lunar day and Earth sits high in the sky.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.blurb: Broad ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache.
sites.why: A long, gently sloping ridge with some of the best continuous illumination near the pole and a workable Earth horizon.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
sites.blurb: Sunlit rim of de Gerlache crater, near 89.7°S.
sites.why: Strong solar access, but the local ridge that gives it light also occludes Earth for part of the libration cycle.

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.why: Elevation buys illumination: a high point sees the Sun over terrain that shadows the surrounding basin.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.blurb: An 8 km massif at 86°S, far from the pole itself.
sites.why: Among the most persistently lit terrain on the Moon, but Earth is low on the horizon and easily lost behind the massif.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.why: A balanced site: moderate slopes, reasonable illumination, and access to permanently shadowed terrain without living in it.

sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
sites.blurb: High plateau west of the pole, ~85.5°S.
sites.why: Broad, relatively flat high ground with excellent solar exposure and a long horizon — good for a power-rich surface asset.

sites.name: de Gerlache–Kocher Massif
sites.blurb: Massif between de Gerlache and Kocher craters.
sites.why: Complex terrain: the trade between solar exposure and Earth line of sight changes sharply over a few hundred metres.

sites.name: Apollo 11 · Tranquility Base
sites.why: A useful calibration point: near-equatorial Sun, Earth high overhead, and no polar lighting drama. Geometry is exact; terrain is spherical here.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 · Von Kármán
sites.why: Far-side geometry means Earth is permanently below the horizon: the canonical case for why a relay is mandatory.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 · Shiv Shakti
sites.why: The highest-latitude successful landing to date; a natural benchmark for how much terrain drives the polar lighting problem.

sites.name: Mons Mouton · CLPS target
sites.why: A near-polar CLPS target used here for geometric context; a dedicated 5 m DEM would be required before using it for real site selection.
